rationale:
Evidence: the best raced design is iteration 7 (score 58.17; oval 63.49, s-bend 66.85, slalom 44.19; no completions). Its telemetry shows 2 line-loss events per run on the oval, 1 on the s-bend and slalom, and steering_oscillation of 0.149 to 0.169. Progress is 0.11 to 0.16. Every run still ends off_track.

What I accepted from the round-1 critique: (1) My draft's stated baseline was wrong. It attributed the gain to values that were never raced (wheel_track 0.14, kp 3.0, kd 1.0, mass 0.6, sensor_size 0.016). I reject that draft. (2) kd 1.5 is not supported. The loop gives kd x 100 turn units per unit of signal change per step, so kd 1.5 amplifies sensor noise. Earlier kd changes did not show damping, and the oscillation tracked kp and sensor geometry instead. I drop kd 1.5 and keep kd 0.1. (3) Reducing the steering gain (wheel_track 0.16 with kp 3.0) is unquantified and is the same direction as the iteration 2 under-steering failure. I drop it. (4) The draft changed several variables at once, so the next race could not be attributed. I return to the raced 58.17 design.

What I rejected from the critique: I did not treat the oval as unexplainable. The oval is an open question, and I do not claim to fix it here.

What I changed: one variable only, base_speed 1.5 to 1.3. Progress, not completion, is the only reachable score term. Completion has not occurred on any track, and the 1.5 m/s finish requirement is unmeasured. Lowering speed reduces the drive demand and gives the loop more time per bend, which may cut the 1 to 2 line-loss events. The cost is a possible loss of progress if the robot stalls, and the completion-time term is already zero.

Falsifiable targets relative to 58.17: line_loss_events at or below 1 on every track; oval max_error below 0.06; steering_oscillation not above 0.16; progress at or above 0.16 on all tracks.

Reversal rule: if the score falls below 58.17, or any track's progress falls, return base_speed to 1.5. If line-loss counts stay at 2 on the oval with progress unchanged, speed is not the cause, and the next single change should target the oval start transient rather than gains.
